newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian metals - Downtrend seen in nickel, tin prices.
newsitem.headline: Indian metals - Downtrend seen in nickel, tin prices.

text.p: Continuing imports of nickel and tin are expected to push prices down further on local non-ferrous metals markets in the next few days, dealers said on Wednesday.
"There's little demand for these metals but still imports are coming without any let-up," said Sharad Parikh, Bombay Metal Exchange president.
"I expect nickel prices to fall further," he said. Nickel and tin lost 400 rupees and 100 rupees per quintal respectively in the week to June 25.

Parikh said a drop in nickel and tin prices on the London Metal Exchange (LME) prompted imports by Indian traders. Imports of tin and nickel from Russia and Malaysia had also been arriving in the market, he said.
"Importers are taking advantage of a downtrend in international prices," Parikh said. "They are hoping that nickel prices will improve in the near future."
Traders sid copper and zinc improved in line with LME trends.
The state-owned Hindustan Copper Ltd raised the price of copper cathods by 100 rupees per quintal (100 kg) and of wire rods by 500 rupees per quintal.
The government-run Hindustan Zinc Ltd had also raised the price of zinc ingots by 250 rupees per quintal.
In the week to Wednesday, nickel fell 900 rupees to 34,500 rupees per quintal. Tin was down 600 rupees to 29,800 rupees per quintal.

Copper was up 25 rupees at 13,875 rupees per quintal. Zinc gained 50 rupees to 8,150 rupees per quintal. Aluminium and lead were unchanged at 7,700 rupees per quintal and 4,100 rupees per quintal respectively.
